q1066.s: Naval superiority of the British. Select the correct answer from the codes given below. Codes: (a) Only 1 (b) Only 2 (c) Both 1 and 2 (d) Neither 1 nor 2 U.P.R.O. / A.R.O. (Pre) (Re-Exam) 2016 Ans (c) There were many causes of the success of the British in India. Naval superiority, getting huge wealth and manpower from Bengal, better internal coordination among British army etc. were few of them. East India Company and Nawabs of Bengal *Murshid Quli Khan was the last Governor of Bengal who was independently appointed by Mughal King. Murshid Quli Khan shifted his Capital to Maksudabad from Dhaka and named it Murshidabad. He started Izara System in the land settlement. * Alivardi Khan (1740-1756 A.D.) comparing Europeans with the Honeybees, said that if they are left undisturbed, they will give you honey, and if try to disturb them they will bite you till death. *After the death of Alivardi Khan, his grandson Siraj-ud-Daula succeeded to the throne of Bengal. The Black Hole tragedy took place during his reign on 20 th June 1756 A.D. According to one of the 23 survivors, J.Z. Holwell, 146 English prisoners were put in a cell with a dimension of 18 feet in length and 14 feet 10 inches in breadth. 123 of them died due to suffocation and only 23 survived. This incident is known as Black Hole tragedy. Contemporary Muslim historian Ghulam Hussain in his book ‘Siyar-ul- Mutakherin’ has not mentioned this incident. *Robert Clive is known as the founder of the English Empire in India who defeated the forces of Bengal’s Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula in the Battle of Plassey (presently known as Palasi) on 23 rd June, 1757 A.D. and sown the seeds of British rule in India. The Battleﬁ eld of Plassey is situated on the Banks of Bhagirathi River in Nadia district of West Bengal. Robert Clive was the Governor in 1758- 60 A.D. and 1765-67 A.D. in India. During this period he signed Allahabad Treaty with Nawab of Awadh Shuja-ud-Daula and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II During his governorship White Mutiny broke out among English soldiers.* Plundering of resources of Bengal by the British Company was started during Clive’s governorship. *Mir Qasim (1760-63 A.D.) was the ablest among the successors of Alivardi Khan. As a ‘Faujdar’ of Poornia and Rangpur, Mir Qasim had already proven his ability. To save his courtiers from repeated conspiracies by Britishers and to avoid interference from Englishmen, Mir Qasim shifted his Capital to Munger from Murshidabad so as to stay away from Calcutta. He consolidated his army using European methods. He made arrangements in Munger for the manufacturing of Matchlock guns. Mir Qasim also took some brave steps so as to improve the economic conditions in Bengal. The of ﬁ cers involved in embezzlement were ﬁ ned heavily, some new taxes were introduced *The Combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula (Nawab of Awadh), and Mughal King Shah Alam II were defeated by Britishers in the Battle of Buxar on 22/23 October, 1764 AD. English army was led by Hector Munro. Henry Vansittart was the then Governor of Bengal. This victory of Britishers made the English a great power in northern India and contenders for supremacy over the whole country. The area up to Allahabad was now under the British and the door of Delhi was now open for British. Battle of Buxar changed the course of Indian History. During this battle, Mir Jafar was Nawab of Bengal and Delhi was ruled by Shah Alam II. By the treaties of Allahabad (August, 1765) Shah Alam II agreed to reside at Allahabad, under the company’s protection. Nawab Shuja-ud-Daula surrendered Allahabad and Kora to Emperor Shah Alam II. *Shah Alam II issued a decree granting Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the East India Company. *Robert Clive became the governor of Bengal and started Dual government system in Bengal. *The Company appointed two deputy Diwans, Mohammad Raza Khan for Bengal and Raja Shitab Roy for Bihar to exercise Diwani functions. Rohilla Sardar Ghulam Qadir annexed Delhi in July 1788, and August 1788, he ousted Shah Alam II and made him blind. During the time of Shah Alam II in 1803, Delhi fell completely to East India Company. Shah Alam II and his two successors Akbar II (1806-37 AD) and Bahadur Shah II (1837-57 AD) were mere pensioners of the East India Company. *The British came to Sylhet (then Sylhet was part of Bengal Presidency) in 1765 AD after acquiring the Diwani right of Bengal. After the War of Burma, David Scott tried to connect Assam (Brahmaputra Valley) with Sylhet through roads to Jaintia and Garo Hill areas, but faced a very tough resistance from the Khasi tribes who lived in these areas under the leadership of Tirot Sing. *K.M. Panikar said that from 1757 to 1773 AD the Company made Bengal a ‘State of Robbers’.

q1169.s: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R) : Assertion (A) : The British Government introduced different land revenue system in different part of India. Reason (R) : It led to create different classes in Indi- an peasantry. Select the correct answer from the codes given below. Codes : (a) Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A) (b) Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A) (c) (A) is true but (R) is false (d) (A) is false but (R) is true U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2020 Ans (a) British government followed different land revenue systems in different parts of India. These systems were: Permanent Settlement, Ryotwari & Mahalwari. Permanent Settlement was introduced in Bengal, Bihar, Odisha & Varanasi of U.P. Under this system around 19% area of entire British India was included. Ryotwari (approx. 51% area) system was in Madras, some parts of Mumbai, Assam, Coorg. Mahalwari (around 30% of the area) system around was in U.P, Central Province, Punjab. Hence, it is clear that because of this, different classes were created in Indian peasantry. Hence, option (a) is correct.
